Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: cleaned-up player character sprite for LAST EMBER, a dark top-down neon survival game. Edit the supplied sprite as the baseline. Keep its recognizable warm white circular ember core, amber-orange outer fire, facing to the RIGHT with the tail streaming LEFT, and true orthographic overhead view. Improve its readability as the controlled player against dark navy and similarly orange enemies/bullets at approximately 32 x 18 CSS pixels in mobile play. The body must read instantly as hot fire with a distinct directional flame shape, even at tiny scale.

Make the tail substantially bolder. Use precisely TWO prominent broad tapering tongues swept to the left, deliberately staggered vertically with one big clean cutout between them, plus one small stepped notch near the upper rim. The two tapering silhouettes and negative space must remain apparent after downsampling. Maintain a visible round pale cream core at roughly x=59%, y=50% of the canvas with a diameter around 30% of the square image. Use a bright gold shoulder around the cream core, vibrant tangerine tail, deep burnt orange outside contour, and minimal restrained red at the left tips. The right front forms a compact pointed gold snout. Keep the main core and its center filled. Replace faint, muddy gradient shading with a few strongly separated, confident curved color shapes and restrained inner shading. Stylized hand-painted arcade flame, with a crisp outer cutout and generous padding; not a jet or spacecraft.

Output exactly one square image with true transparent background, existing sprite's wide horizontal footprint and center height, clear edges. Do not bake in exterior bloom, flare or glare. No loose particles, streaks outside the flame, cast shadow, perspective, ground, background color, checkerboard, badge, text, symbols, tiles, or watermark.
